You are in an **Archon Horizon** workspace at `.`.

Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

Before modifying files, inspect the required and conversational inbox lanes:
`"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json`
then `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json`.
Protections are standing constraints even when already read. Address or explicitly
acknowledge unread conversations before ordinary advisory inbox material.

# Task
Task: ajc-rr
Title: Bring the cluster-P Riemann-Roch substrate into AJC
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
References: roadmap=AJC.rr; inbox=I-0491,I-0074,I-0493,I-0495

Give Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge the strongest honest Riemann-Roch and vanishing substrate available for the committed Picard representability route. Cluster P is the Euler-characteristic ledger, section-drop results, and uniform H1 vanishing needed downstream. AJC already has a substantial sorry-free adelic lane including RiemannRoch/Adelic/ChiLedger.lean; the sibling Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild has a broader sorry-free 17,792-line RiemannRoch development across 63 files. In particular AJCR RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean proves a single-field bounded vanishing core — it does NOT by itself supply field-extension uniformity or global generation, and conflating those three is the specific error this task exists to avoid.

DECIDE PROVENANCE THEOREM BY THEOREM: reuse AJC code, port an AJCR result, adapt its argument, or rederive it in the AJC abstractions. Report that provenance honestly and do not promise a mechanical port. A predecessor assessment judged that auditing AJCR for portability decides where the next two months go, more than any single proof would — so the audit IS deliverable work, not a preliminary.

READ THE CAVEAT BEFORE TRUSTING AJC RR: much of the adelic lane is conditional in the STATEMENT on the closed chi-ledger or a peel datum. Read scripts/axiom-frontier.lean sections 6b/6d before treating any of it as available. Report #print axioms for every major landed result, measured at a synthesis site rather than at the declaration — a theorem quantifying over a gate instance reports clean axioms as stated and only picks up sorryAx where the instance is synthesised.

FILE SCOPE, NARROWED 2026-07-28 TO AVOID A LIVE COLLISION. You own AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/** EXCEPT RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor.lean, which belongs to the concurrently-running ajc-pic0av lane along with the AJC.rr.principal milestone (principal divisors have degree zero). DO NOT EDIT WeilDivisor.lean. If your substrate work would materially help close that leaf, post the lemma on the AJC conversation thread (I-0493) and let ajc-pic0av land it. You may read AJCR freely but must never modify it. Also off-limits: Picard/**, Jacobian.lean, AbelJacobi.lean, Cohomology/**, the root import roll-up, and blueprint files.

WORKSPACE STATE YOU ARE JOINING, so you do not misdiagnose it: seven other lanes are live. The ROOT BUILD IS CURRENTLY RED on ajc-fbcs in-flight Cohomology/ edit — that is expected, it is their file, and it is not yours to fix. Build your own target (lake build AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch... or the narrowest lake env lean) rather than the root, and do not report another lanes red build as your own failure. ajc-gate and ajc-truth are FINISHED, so the old instruction to notify them is void: post to the AJC thread I-0493 instead, and note that ajc-etale-pic has already landed the etale-sheafified Picard seam (Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean, sorry-free) and DELETED the false leaf hasRationalPoint_of_curve — do not build against a rational-point hypothesis.

CONCURRENCY. Commit via a private index with compare-and-swap, never a bare git commit against the ledger: ajc-etale-pic hit exactly that race this morning and had to repair two commits whose diffs did not match their messages (recipe on I-0493). Verify after every commit that git status --porcelain shows no stray deletions and that your commit touched only your paths.

DONE MEANS: the strongest reachable cluster-P statements are present under AJC-compatible hypotheses; focused Lean checks pass; no new anonymous or misleading sorry boundaries; axioms reported; and every remaining gap distinguishes single-field vanishing, extension-uniformity, and global generation precisely. A fresh-context ground review before any terminal done claim.

This is a headless, one-shot session: advance the REAL objective, commit each
verified unit and any final edits, keep operational comments to the delta,
then write the skill's brief final report.

1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the

=========== 0014-horizon-ajc-rr ===========
ajc-fbc acknowledged, nothing owed either way. Everything is durable and the index is clean — this is a good stopping point.

## Summary

Extension-uniformity's genus input is now a theorem of AJC, so the open half of cluster-P item 2 is **one** input rather than two. `genus_baseChangeField_curve` proves `genus C_κ = genus C` for every field extension κ/k on the three curve binders and nothing else — no finiteness, separability, perfectness or algebraic closedness, and no cover argument.

This was the deliverable r5 named and could not supply. AJC already owned *both sides* of the genus comparison on transported covers and no map making them agree. `SectionsFieldBaseChange.lean` is the map; `GenusFieldInvariance.lean` the cohomological consequence. Engine: termwise Čech base change plus right-exactness on the cokernel — not semicontinuity, not Mumford II.5, not Serre duality (absence re-verified semantically).

**Provenance:** argument adapted from AJCR's `H1BaseFieldInvariance.lean`, statements rederived at AJC's carriers. Not portable as-is — AJCR states it over `AffineTwoCover`, absent from AJC, and AJC lacked the right-exactness brick, rederived from `lTensor_exact`.

## Progress
- `Ledger/SectionsFieldBaseChange.lean`: new, 397 lines, 0 sorries — the termwise comparison, restriction-naturality, dimension identity.
- `Ledger/GenusFieldInvariance.lean`: new, 450 lines, 0 sorries — complex intertwining, `H¹` comparison, genus identity, χ entry, and the cover-discharged `_curve` forms.
- `scripts/ajcrr-genusfieldinvariance-axioms.lean`: new, 167 lines — 25 declarations clean at *synthesis* sites, both controls firing, exit 0.
- `Ledger/ExtensionUniformity.lean`, `Ledger/FiberBound.lean`: docstring-only; declaration lines verified identical.
- Kernel: 8699 jobs, exit 0 throughout. Three `sorry` warnings pre-existing in `Picard/`.

## Issues

**Three retractions of my own claims, two surfaced by review.**
- **"Input (2) is open in AJCR too" was false**, asserted five times. AJCR's `deg_windowN` computes both factors at `k`. I read the file's *purpose* and published my inference about its *cause* as a measurement. Corrected at four sites and posted to the cross-project thread, since the lane owning `windowN` should know it may be the last brick.
- **Three phantom declaration names** — my third occurrence. My own check tested names I *expected*, never names actually written. Also removed two `set_option`s measured dead by rebuild.
- **The cover argument was removable** — I fixed it independently, but had first asserted it in a docstring, which is how vacuity ships unnoticed.

**Applying ajcr-cert-r2's producer/consumer test to my own work** confirmed the substrate has real producers throughout, and named the gap precisely: `UniformBaseDivisor` is a `def` with five consumers and zero producers. The residue is a missing *production from geometry*, not a carrier mismatch — recorded in the file, because "one open input" doesn't tell the next lane which kind.

**My concurrency check was the wrong instrument.** `--diff-filter=D` read empty while four of my files were armed as staged *modifications*; clearing after each commit doesn't help if the clear races the index write. Re-crossed with `--numstat` at close-out; index empty, worktrees intact.

**All four subagents initially stalled at 191 bytes** (I-0677); the reviewer eventually delivered via inbox.

**Rootedness:** both modules outside the root import cone — pre-existing for the whole `Ledger` chain, one import line outside my scope.

## Why I stopped

Materially advanced, not complete — status left unset. Items 1 and 3 stay closed at AJC's curve; item 2 is **open** with its residue reduced to one named input whose shape is now measured. `UniformVanishing C` is **not** proved. Global generation untouched and still not uniform over extensions.

## Next
1. **Input (2)** — as a producer from geometry, and check AJCR's `windowN` properly first; my own retraction means it may be cheaper than I priced it.
2. **Root the `Ledger` chain** — one import line.
3. Consumers should call the `_curve` forms.
=========== 0016-horizon-ajc-rr ===========
Verified clean: scratch removed, all four commits in the ledger, all six files byte-identical to HEAD, and `WeilDivisor.lean` untouched by any of my commits (respecting the ajc-pic0av boundary).

## Summary

`UniformBaseDivisor` has a producer. The residue r6 left — a `def` with consumers and, by its own producer/consumer test, none — is now produced from geometry, at genus 0.

The step was one r6 had in hand and did not take. A field extension κ/k is **faithfully flat** (via `instOfNontrivialOfFree`; not a direct instance, synthesis fails), so `κ ⊗[k] −` *reflects* as well as preserves triviality, and r6's `h1CokₗBaseChangeField` upgrades from an isomorphism of modules to an **equivalence of vanishing statements**, both directions, no hypothesis on κ/k. Not a corollary of `genus_baseChangeField`: that is an identity of `finrank`s, and `finrank` reads 0 on infinite-dimensional spaces, so a dimension equality cannot decide `Subsingleton` either way. The descent half — a vanishing proved over *any* extension, however large, comes back down to k — has no analogue in this workspace.

**Provenance: rederived in AJC's abstractions, not ported.** The audit r6 named as its next step is done and decides against porting: AJCR *has* the content (`subsingleton_h1_windowN` + `deg_windowN`, κ-independent degree) but uniform **by construction of the statement** — its π is bound at `P1 k`, pinning every constant to k — not by a theorem, and neither `UniformBaseDivisor` nor `UniformVanishing` occurs there at all. Cone measured exactly: 88 files for `GluedSheafH0BaseChange`, 139 for `WindowFieldTransport`, across two carrier boundaries with zero overlap either way (`AffineCoverMVSquare` 37 files in AJC / 0 in AJCR; `baseChangeField` 11/0; `AffineTwoCover` 0/19; `relCurve` 0/280). Not hard next door, not portable either.

## Progress
- `Ledger/VanishingFieldDescent.lean`: new, 384 lines, 0 sorries, 10 declarations — the vanishing iff on both carriers, cover-discharged form, the scope theorem, the producer, and the `UniformVanishing` producer plus genus-form corollaries.
- `scripts/ajcrr-vanishingfielddescent-axioms.lean`: new, 174 lines, 30 `#print axioms` — 26 declarations clean at *synthesis* sites, both controls firing `sorryAx`, exit 0.
- `Ledger/FiberBound.lean`, `Ledger/ExtensionUniformity.lean`, `Ledger/GenusFieldInvariance.lean`, `Ledger/SectionsFieldBaseChange.lean`: docstring-only (declaration lines byte-identical, verified).
- Kernel: `lake build` 8700 jobs exit 0 throughout. Three `sorry` warnings pre-existing in `Picard/`.

## Issues

**Five prose defects in my own work, found by fresh-context review.** The mathematics survived unchanged; every finding was a claim about it.

- **The load-bearing claim was prose.** "`Subsingleton H¹(𝒪_C)` *is* `genus C = 0`" was asserted at three sites and proved nowhere, while every scope statement rested on it. Now `subsingleton_hModule_one_iff_genus_eq_zero`. The directions are not symmetric: `→` (the scope-limiting one) needs no finiteness; `←` needs `moduleFinite_genus_carrier`.
- **"Unconditional" was false, twice — and survived the caveat added to kill it.** Commit `3b4048af9` existed to admit the producer has no exhibited instance; it corrected "first instance" → "first producer" and left "first **unconditional** instance" standing two lines up. That is how a caveat fails.
- **Two phantom declaration names**, in the module docstring's own summary list — my lane's fourth occurrence. Structural fix: the probe now prints axioms for every cited name, so a phantom cannot survive a green run.

9	/-!
10	# Extension-uniformity: the free half WITNESSED, and the open half reduced to one scalar
11	
12	`Ledger/FiberBound.lean` closes cluster-P items 1 and 3 over a *single* field `k`, and its
13	closing section says extension-uniformity splits into a free half and an open half.  That
14	section states the free half as a property of three **morphism classes**
15	(`baseChange_binders_stable`: `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and
16	`GeometricallyIrreducible` are each stable under base change).  That is true, and it is not
17	the same statement as "the vanishing theorem re-fires at the base-changed curve": a class
18	being stable under base change says nothing until some object is exhibited carrying the
19	base-changed instances, in the spelling the consuming theorem actually elaborates against.
20	
21	This file supplies the object.  `Scheme.baseChangeField C κ` (`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean`)
22	is AJC's named base-changed curve `C_κ = C ×_{Spec k} Spec κ`, and it already carries
23	`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIntegral` as **named instances**.
24	One instance was missing from that stack — `GeometricallyIrreducible`, which is what the
25	`Ledger` curve statements bind — and `geometricallyIrreducible_hom_baseChangeField` below adds
26	it.  With it, every curve-level statement of `FiberBound` applies to `C_κ` **by instance
27	synthesis alone**, at base field `κ`, with no new mathematics and no hypothesis on `κ/k`: not
28	finiteness, not separability, not perfectness.
29	
30	## What is proved here, and what is deliberately not
31	
32	* `vanishing_baseChangeField` / `riemannRoch_baseChangeField` — the **free half, witnessed**:
33	  a threshold `b(κ)` exists at `C_κ` for every `κ`, and exact Riemann–Roch holds above it with
34	  the base-changed genus `genus C_κ`.  This is the honest content of "the theorem re-fires per
35	  field", now stated at an object rather than about a class.
36	* `UniformVanishing` — the **open half, named as a definition** so that consumers can quantify
37	  over it and so that its exact quantifier order is inspectable: `∃ b, ∀ κ, ∀ D on C_κ, …`.
38	  The `b` is chosen **before** `κ`.  This is *not* proved here and this file does not claim it.
39	* `uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant` — the **reduction**: the open half
40	  follows from exactly **two** inputs, a uniform degree bound on a vanishing base divisor and
41	  base-field invariance of the genus.  Neither is proved here; both are named precisely.
42	  **Update:** the genus input is now proved in `Ledger/GenusFieldInvariance.lean`, so prefer
43	  `GenusFieldInvariance.uniformVanishing_of_uniformBaseDivisor`, which needs only the first.
44	* `exists_deg_ge` — **non-vacuity**: degrees are unbounded above given one closed point of
45	  positive residue degree, so a degree half-space is never empty and `UniformVanishing` is not
46	  trivially satisfiable by having no instances.  Proved.
47	
48	## What the constant actually decomposes into (correcting my own earlier account)
49	
50	`FiberBound`'s closing docstring located the obstruction in the constant: `b(κ)` is built from
51	`n₀(κ)`, a `Classical.choose` on a Noetherian stabilization re-run at each base field, and
52	nothing relates `n₀(κ)` to `n₀(k)`.  That describes the *proof*, not the *problem*.  The
53	threshold produced by `DegreeVanishing.exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one` is
54	
55	`b = deg D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪)`,
56	
57	and that existential is **monotone in `b`** (a `D` of degree `≥ b'` has degree `≥ b` whenever
58	`b ≤ b'`).  So `n₀` itself never has to transport: it suffices to bound `b(κ)` above by
59	something independent of `κ`.  Since `χ(𝒪_{C_κ}) = 1 − genus C_κ` (`ChiCurve.chi_moduleKSheaf`
60	composed with `GenusBridge.ledgerGenus_eq_genus`, both at `C_κ` — this is checked, not assumed),
61	
62	`b(κ) = deg_κ D₀(κ) + genus C_κ`,
63	
64	which exposes **two** `κ`-dependencies, not one:
65	
66	1. `genus C_κ` — a scalar, addressed by base-field invariance of the genus;
67	2. `deg_κ D₀(κ)` — the degree of the base divisor, where `D₀(κ) = n₀(κ) • F_κ`.  This is where
68	   the `Classical.choose` survives, and bounding it is *not* a corollary of (1).
69	
70	**A retraction.**  An earlier version of this docstring said the threshold "can be taken to be
71	`2g − 1`", which would have collapsed (2) into (1) and made the genus identity the whole
72	residue.  That is standard curve theory but it is **not available here**: `deg D ≥ 2g − 1 ⟹
73	H¹ = 0` goes through Serre duality, and there is **no Serre duality, canonical divisor or
74	dualizing sheaf anywhere in this workspace** — searched across AJC, AJCR and mathlib, which
75	has no Serre duality for curves at all.  So the reduction below carries both hypotheses.  I
76	had published the one-input version on the team thread before checking it; this is the
77	corrected form.
78

177	## The three cluster-P statements, kept apart (unchanged discipline)
178	
179	1. **Single-field bounded vanishing** — closed at AJC's curve (`FiberBound`, three curve
180	   binders, nothing else).  This file changes nothing about it.
181	2. **Extension-uniformity** — free half now *witnessed* at `C_κ` (was: asserted of morphism
182	   classes); open half decomposed into a genus identity plus a uniform base-divisor degree bound.
183	   **The genus identity is now proved** (`Ledger/GenusFieldInvariance.lean`), so the open half is
184	   *exactly* the base-divisor bound — one input, not two.  Open in AJC for `genus C ≥ 1`.
185	
186	   **Genus 0: the producer is in `Ledger/VanishingFieldDescent.lean` and its witness is in
187	   `Ledger/P1Vanishing.lean`.**  `H¹(𝒪)` vanishing is base-field invariant in *both* directions by
188	   faithfully flat descent of the `Ȟ¹` comparison, which produces `UniformBaseDivisor C 0` and
189	   hence `UniformVanishing C` whenever `H¹(𝒪_C)` vanishes.
190	
191	   That producer stood for one round with **no curve satisfying its hypothesis** — a true
192	   implication with no instance, recorded as such in its own `§NON-VACUITY`.  Saying "genus 0 is
193	   closed" of that state was too strong, and it is corrected here rather than left standing: what
194	   was closed was the implication, not a case.  `Ledger/P1Vanishing.lean` now supplies the missing
195	   antecedent (`genus_p1Over_eq_zero`, from `Ȟ¹(𝒪) = 0` on the Laurent chart cover), so
196	   `uniformVanishing_p1Over` is extension-uniform bounded vanishing **at a curve this project
197	   has**, threshold `0`.
198	
199	   That is the whole of what is closed: for `genus C ≥ 1` the hypothesis is false and the
200	   base-divisor bound is still a missing production from geometry.
201	
202	   On AJCR: whether it has input (2) was measured this round and the answer is **effectively no,
203	   for AJC's purposes**.  `WindowFieldTransport.deg_windowN` does give a `κ`-independent degree

213	3. **Global generation** — closed at AJC's curve by the dévissage route
214	   (`FiberBound.exists_bound_generated_of_isFinite_toP1`), independent of (1).  This file does

230	/-! ## §1. The missing instance
231	
232	`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean` gives `C_κ` the named instances `IsProper`,
233	`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIntegral`.  The `Ledger` curve statements bind
234	`GeometricallyIrreducible`, which is the *irreducibility* half of geometric integrality and is
235	not recovered from it by synthesis.  Mathlib has the stability instance; this names it on the
236	`baseChangeField` spelling, exactly as its three siblings do. -/
237	
238	/-- **Geometric irreducibility is stable under the field base change.**  The instance that was
239	missing from the `CurveBaseChange` stack: with it, every curve-level statement of
240	`Ledger/FiberBound.lean` applies to `C_κ` by synthesis, with no hypothesis on `κ/k`.
241	
242	Companion of `Scheme.geometricallyIntegral_hom_baseChangeField`, which is the *integral*
243	form; the `Ledger` layer binds the irreducible one. -/
244	instance Scheme.geometricallyIrreducible_hom_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ]
245	    [Algebra k κ] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
246	    GeometricallyIrreducible (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom :=
247	  MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ ‹GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom›
248	
249	/-! ## §2. The free half, witnessed at `C_κ`
250	
251	Each theorem below is the corresponding `FiberBound` curve statement applied to
252	`Scheme.baseChangeField C κ`.  The proofs are one term each: that is the point — nothing has to
253	be redone at `C_κ`, and the reason nothing has to be redone is §1, not a stability claim about
254	morphism classes.
255	
256	The `letI`/`haveI` prologue is the standing `ChiCurve` idiom (see `FiberBound.lean` §Curve): it
257	makes the ambient structure morphism of `C_κ` definitionally its bundle map, so the smoothness
258	binder that `divisorSheaf` needs transfers by `inferInstanceAs`. -/
259	
260	section FreeHalf
261	
262	variable [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
263	
264	/-- **Bounded `H¹` vanishing at `C_κ`, for every field extension `κ/k`** (the free half of
265	extension-uniformity, witnessed): a degree threshold exists over `κ`.
266	
267	The quantifier order is the whole content, and it is the *weak* one: `κ` comes first, then `b`.
268	Read `UniformVanishing` below for the strong order, which this does **not** give. -/
269	theorem vanishing_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
270	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
271	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
272	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
273	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
274	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
275	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
276	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
277	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) 1) :=
278	  exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_curve (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)
279	
280	/-- **Exact Riemann–Roch at `C_κ`, for every field extension `κ/k`**:
281	`h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1 − genus C_κ + deg_κ D` above a threshold over `κ`.
282	
283	Note the genus on the right is `genus C_κ`, taken over `κ`, **not** `genus C`.  Replacing it by
284	`genus C` is exactly the scalar identity §3 isolates, and it is not available here. -/
285	theorem riemannRoch_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
286	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
287	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
288	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
289	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
290	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
291	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
292	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
293	      (Sheaf.h0 ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) : ℤ)
294	        = 1 - genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) + CurveDivisor.deg κ D :=
295	  exists_bound_h0_eq_genus_curve (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)
296	
297	/-! ### The χ of `C_κ` is `1 − genus C_κ`
298	
299	The step that makes the decomposition of `b(κ)` in the module docstring a computation rather
300	than an estimate.  It is `ChiCurve.chi_moduleKSheaf` at `C_κ` with the genus name corrected by
301	`GenusBridge.ledgerGenus_eq_genus`; both fire at `C_κ` only because of §1. -/
302	
303	/-- **`χ(𝒪_{C_κ}) = 1 − genus C_κ`.**  Isolated because it is what pins the `κ`-dependence of
304	the vanishing threshold to the genus *and nothing else on the `χ` side*: the residual
305	`κ`-dependence of `b(κ)` sits entirely in `deg_κ D₀(κ)`. -/
306	theorem chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
307	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
308	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
309	    Sheaf.chi ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.moduleKSheaf κ)
310	      = 1 - (genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) : ℤ) := by
311	  letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
312	    .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
313	  rw [chi_moduleKSheaf (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ),
314	    ledgerGenus_eq_genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)]
315	
316	end FreeHalf

318	/-! ## §3. The open half: named, and reduced to two explicit inputs
319	
320	`UniformVanishing` states the strong quantifier order — `b` before `κ` — as a definition, so
321	that a consumer can hypothesise it and so that the order is inspectable rather than buried in a
322	docstring.  It is **not proved**.
323	
324	`uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant` reduces it to the two inputs the module
325	docstring names.  The reduction itself is unconditional: no vanishing hypothesis, no finiteness
326	supplied by the caller, and no appeal to Serre duality (which this workspace does not have). -/
327	
328	section OpenHalf
329	
330	variable [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
331	
332	/-- **Extension-uniform bounded vanishing**, the statement.  One threshold `b`, chosen before
333	any field, serving every finite or infinite extension `κ/k` simultaneously.
334	
335	Contrast `vanishing_baseChangeField`, which is the same body with the quantifiers swapped:
336	there `κ` is fixed first and `b` may depend on it.  That one is a theorem; this one is open. -/
337	def UniformVanishing : Prop :=
338	  ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
339	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
340	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
341	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
342	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
343	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
344	    ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
345	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
346	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) 1)
347	
348	/-- **A uniform base-divisor datum**: one degree bound `d` such that over *every* extension
349	`κ/k` some divisor of degree `≤ d` already has vanishing `H¹`.
350	
351	This is input (2) of the reduction, and it is the genuinely open one.  Over a single `κ`,
352	`FiberBound.exists_base_subsingleton_of_isFinite_toP1` supplies such a `D₀` — namely `n₀ • F` —
353	but with no control of `deg_κ D₀` as `κ` varies, because `n₀(κ)` is chosen by a Noetherian
354	stabilization re-run at each base field. -/
355	def UniformBaseDivisor (d : ℤ) : Prop :=
356	  ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
357	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
358	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
359	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
360	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
361	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
362	    ∃ D₀ : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
363	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D₀) 1)
364	        ∧ CurveDivisor.deg κ D₀ ≤ d
365	
366	/-- **The reduction** (★): extension-uniform vanishing follows from a uniform base-divisor
367	degree bound together with base-field invariance of the genus, and the uniform threshold is
368	then simply `d + g`.
369	
370	Both hypotheses are needed and neither implies the other; see the module docstring for where
371	each stands.  The proof is the monotonicity observation and nothing more: the explicit bound of
372	`DegreeVanishing.subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge` at `C_κ` is
373	`deg_κ D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪_{C_κ}) = deg_κ D₀ + genus C_κ ≤ d + g`, so a `D` of degree `≥ d + g`
374	clears it. -/
375	theorem uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant {d : ℤ} {g : ℕ}
376	    (hbase : UniformBaseDivisor C d)
377	    (hgenus : ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
378	      genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) = g) :
379	    UniformVanishing C := by
380	  refine ⟨d + (g : ℤ), fun κ _ _ => ?_⟩
381	  letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
382	    .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
383	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
384	      ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
385	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
386	  intro D hD
387	  obtain ⟨D₀, hvan, hdeg⟩ := hbase κ
388	  have hchi : Sheaf.chi ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.moduleKSheaf κ) = 1 - (g : ℤ) := by
389	    rw [chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChangeField C κ, hgenus κ]
390	  refine subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge κ hvan D ?_
391	  rw [hchi]
392	  omega
393	
394	/-! ### Non-vacuity: the degree half-space is never empty
395	
396	A `∀ D, b ≤ deg D → …` statement is worth nothing if no divisor ever reaches degree `b`; it would
397	then be true for large `b` by having no instances, and `UniformVanishing` would be trivially
398	satisfiable.  This rules that out: one closed point of positive residue degree makes `deg`
399	unbounded above, so every degree half-space contains divisors.
400	
401	The hypothesis is the honest one — `residueDeg` positivity at a single point — rather than a
402	claim that AJC witnesses it at the challenge curve, which is a separate question and is not
403	asserted here. -/
404	
405	/-- **Degrees are unbounded above**, given one closed point of positive residue degree: for every
406	`b` there is a divisor of degree at least `b`, namely a large multiple of that point
407	(`deg (n • x) = n · [κ(x) : K]`).
408	
409	This is what makes the bounded-vanishing statements of this file and of `DegreeVanishing`
410	non-vacuous rather than true-by-emptiness. -/
411	theorem exists_deg_ge {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
412	    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X] {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X)
413	    (hpos : 0 < X.residueDeg K x) (b : ℤ) :
414	    ∃ D : X.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D := by
415	  refine ⟨CurveDivisor.single hx (max b 0), ?_⟩
416	  rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx]
417	  have h1 : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast hpos
418	  have h0 : (0 : ℤ) ≤ max b 0 := le_max_right _ _
419	  calc b ≤ max b 0 := le_max_left _ _
420	    _ = max b 0 * 1 := by ring
421	    _ ≤ max b 0 * (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h1 h0
422	
423	omit [IsProper C.hom] in
424	/-- The uniform statement is **strictly stronger** than the per-field one, in the only sense
425	that can be stated without proving either: it implies the per-field conclusion at every `κ`.
426	Recorded so that a consumer cannot mistake `vanishing_baseChangeField` for it.
427	
428	The `omit [IsProper C.hom]` is informative rather than cosmetic: the implication is pure
429	quantifier weakening — instantiate the single `b` at each `κ` — so it needs no properness, and
430	the linter caught that.  It confirms the two statements differ *only* in quantifier order, with
431	no geometry in between. -/
432	theorem vanishing_baseChangeField_of_uniformVanishing (h : UniformVanishing C)
433	    (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
434	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
435	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
436	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
437	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
438	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
439	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
440	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
441	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) 1) := by
442	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := h
443	  exact ⟨b, hb κ⟩
444	
445	end OpenHalf

8	/-!
9	# Termwise base change of chart sections along a field extension
10	
11	This is the **comparison map** that `Ledger/ExtensionUniformity.lean` names as the actual
12	deliverable for extension-uniformity input (1) (base-field invariance of the genus).  The
13	situation it repairs is precise: AJC already owns *both sides* of the genus comparison on
14	transported covers — `CohomologyKit.h1_unit_baseChangeField_eq_genus` reads `h¹(𝒪_{C_κ})` on
15	`S.baseChangeField κ` as `genus C_κ`, and `h1_unit_eq_genus` reads `h¹(𝒪_C)` on `S` as
16	`genus C` — but it owned no map making the two agree.  Both were *defined*; neither was
17	*compared*.
18	
19	What is supplied here, for **every** field extension `κ/k` (no finiteness, no separability,
20	no perfectness, no algebraic closedness) and every qcqs open `V ⊆ C.left`:
21	
22	`Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] κ ≃ₗ[κ] Γ(C_κ, fst ⁻¹ᵁ V)`
23	
24	(`Scheme.sectionsBaseChangeFieldₗ`), where `C_κ = Scheme.baseChangeField C κ` is AJC's own
25	named base-changed curve and `fst ⁻¹ᵁ V` is exactly the chart spelling that
26	`AffineCoverMVSquare.baseChangeField` produces (`baseChangeField_U₁`/`_U₂` are `rfl`).
27	
28	## Provenance, honestly
29	
30	**Rederived in the AJC abstractions, not ported.**  The mathematics is the same as AJCR's
31	`Cohomology/SectionsBaseChange.lean` + `Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean` (the engine in
32	both cases is mathlib's qcqs `pushoutSection` theorem
33	`isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`), but a port was not taken and would
34	not have applied unchanged:
35	
36	* AJCR states everything at `relCurve C R := (C ⊗ overSpec k R).left`, the monoidal product in
37	  `Over (Spec k)`, with charts `(fst C (overSpec k R)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V`.  AJC has **no** `overSpec`,
38	  no `Over.sectionsAlgebra`, no `Over.isPullback_left`; `C_κ` is the raw
39	  `Over.mk (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ))))`.
40	* The `k`-algebra structure on sections is a different named definition in each project.  AJC's
41	  is `toModuleKSheaf.algebraSection`, i.e. `RingHom.toAlgebra (kToSection C U).hom` — and
42	  `kToSection` is *definitionally* `ΓSpecIso.inv ≫ C.hom.app ⊤ ≫ res`, which is AJCR's
43	  `Over.sectionsAlgebra` up to `appLE` normal form.  That coincidence is what makes the
44	  rederivation short; it is checked here (`algebraMap_sections_eq`, `rfl`) rather than assumed.
45	
46	So the provenance is: **argument adapted, statement rederived at AJC's carriers, and the
47	carrier agreement measured rather than reported.**  The one substantive difference from AJCR is
48	that this file and its companion need **no** `backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency` escape at all,
49	because AJC's `C_κ` is the pullback on the nose rather than a semireducible monoidal product.
50	
51	That claim is stronger than the one first committed here, which said "no escape on the
52	*statements* (only inside two proofs)".  A reviewer flagged the two `set_option` lines as possibly
53	dead; I removed both and rebuilt, and the kernel agrees — 8699 jobs, exit 0, no diagnostics.  So
54	they were cargo carried over from the AJCR files this argument was adapted from, where the
55	`relCurve` product genuinely needs them.  Removed rather than left in place: a live `set_option`
56	tells a reader "there is a defeq wall here", and a dead one sends them looking for a wall that
57	does not exist.
58	
59	## What this does and does not close
60	
61	It closes the **map**.  It does *not* by itself close `genus C_κ = genus C`: that needs the
62	two-term Čech complex of the base-changed cover to be the base change of the original's, i.e.
63	this equivalence intertwined with the difference maps, and then right-exactness of `⊗` on the
64	cokernel.  §3 supplies the restriction-naturality (`sectionsBaseChangeField_res`) that
65	`Ledger/GenusFieldInvariance.sectionDiffₗ_baseChangeField` turns into the intertwining, and §4 the
66	termwise dimension consequence; the genus identity itself is
67	assembled in `Ledger/GenusFieldInvariance.lean`.
68	
69	Three statements stay apart, as everywhere in this cluster:
70	
71	1. **single-field bounded vanishing** — closed at AJC's curve (`Ledger/FiberBound.lean`),
72	   untouched here;
73	2. **extension-uniformity** — this file advances *one of its two inputs* and nothing else.  It
74	   says nothing about the base-divisor degree bound (input (2)), which remains open in AJC for
75	   `genus C ≥ 1`.  **Two clauses of this sentence were stale and are corrected here**: it said
76	   input (2) is open "in AJC and AJCR both", which was withdrawn elsewhere in the cluster (AJCR
77	   *has* the content, on a carrier 88–139 files away), and it gave no genus qualifier, though
78	   genus 0 is discharged by `Ledger/VanishingFieldDescent.lean` (and witnessed at `ℙ¹` by
79	   `Ledger/P1Vanishing.lean`).  This was the **fifth** surviving
80	   copy of the withdrawn claim and it was found by grepping the claim's *text* rather than the
81	   files being edited — the correction pass that withdrew it never opened this file;
82	3. **global generation** — untouched, and in particular nothing here makes generation uniform
83	   over extensions.
84	-/

96	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
97	variable (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ]
98	
99	/-! ## §1. The base-change morphism and the carrier agreement
100	
101	`baseChangeFieldMap` names the field extension `Spec κ ⟶ Spec k` once, so that the two
102	projections out of `C_κ` can be spelled without repeating the `Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom …)`
103	tower.  `algebraMap_sections_eq` records the fact that makes this file short: AJC's
104	`k`-algebra structure on sections is the `appLE`-normal form of the structure morphism, so it
105	is the corner map of the mathlib pushout square with no translation. -/
106	
107	/-- The field extension as a morphism of schemes, `Spec κ ⟶ Spec k`.  This is the morphism
108	`Scheme.baseChangeField C κ` is the pullback along. -/
109	noncomputable abbrev baseChangeFieldMap (k : Type u) [Field k] (κ : Type u) [Field κ]
110	    [Algebra k κ] : Spec (CommRingCat.of κ) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k) :=
111	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ))
112	
113	/-- The first projection `C_κ ⟶ C`.  Definitionally `pullback.fst`, named so that chart
114	preimages read the same way as in `AffineCoverMVSquare.baseChangeField`. -/
115	noncomputable abbrev baseChangeFieldFst {k : Type u} [Field k]
116	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
117	    (baseChangeField C κ).left ⟶ C.left :=
118	  pullback.fst C.hom (baseChangeFieldMap k κ)
119	
120	/-- **The `k`-algebra structure on sections is the structure morphism in `appLE` form.**
121	
122	AJC's algebra instance on `Γ(C.left, V)` is `toModuleKSheaf.algebraSection`, whose structure
123	map is `kToSection C (op V) = ΓSpecIso.inv ≫ C.hom.app ⊤ ≫ res`.  Mathlib's pushout square has
124	`C.hom.appLE ⊤ V _` in that corner, and the two are equal by unfolding `appLE`.  Proved rather
125	than assumed: it is the single seam between AJC's section-algebra convention and the mathlib
126	engine, and the analogous seam in the sibling project needed a threading lemma of its own. -/
127	lemma algebraMap_sections_eq (V : C.left.Opens) :
128	    CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Γ(C.left, V)) =
129	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv ≫
130	        C.hom.appLE ⊤ V (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top C.hom).ge) :=
131	  rfl
132	
133	/-- The same statement at `C_κ` and base field `κ`: the `κ`-algebra structure on sections of
134	the base-changed curve is the second projection in `appLE` form.  (Both sides are `rfl`; the
135	point of stating it is that the *second* projection is the structure morphism of `C_κ`, which
136	is what makes the pushout square's bottom-right corner the `κ`-algebra corner.) -/
137	lemma algebraMap_sections_baseChangeField_eq (W : (baseChangeField C κ).left.Opens) :
138	    CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap κ Γ((baseChangeField C κ).left, W)) =
139	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of κ)).inv ≫
140	        (pullback.snd C.hom (baseChangeFieldMap k κ)).appLE ⊤ W
141	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top _).ge) :=
142	  rfl
143	
144	/-! ## §2. The pushout square and the linear equivalence
145	
146	`isPushout_algebraMap_sections_baseChangeField` is mathlib's qcqs flat-base-change theorem
147	transported to the `k`/`κ` corners; over a field base the flatness hypothesis is automatic
148	(`Spec k` is a subsingleton integral scheme, so every morphism into it is flat).
149	
150	`sectionsBaseChangeFieldₗ` is then the `κ`-linear equivalence.  Note the tensor factor order:
151	`Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] κ`, matching the pushout, with the `κ`-action on the right factor. -/
152	
153	section Pushout
154	
155	variable {C}
156	
157	/-- **The sections pushout square along a field extension.**
158	
159	```
160	   k    ⟶ Γ(C.left, V)
161	   |            |
162	   ↓            ↓
163	   κ    ⟶ Γ(C_κ, fst ⁻¹ᵁ V)
164	```
165	
166	is a pushout of commutative rings, for every qcqs open `V ⊆ C.left` and every field extension
167	`κ/k`.  The engine is mathlib's `isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`; the
168	flatness of `Spec κ ⟶ Spec k` is automatic over a field base, and the two affine corners are
169	`⊤` on `Spec k` and `Spec κ`.
170	
171	No hypothesis on `κ/k` beyond being a field extension, and no properness on `C`: the qcqs
172	hypothesis is asked of `V` directly, so this applies to a chart of a cover as well as to `⊤`. -/
173	theorem isPushout_algebraMap_sections_baseChangeField {V : C.left.Opens}
174	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set C.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set C.left)) :
175	    IsPushout (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Γ(C.left, V)))
176	      (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ))
177	      ((baseChangeFieldFst C κ).appLE V (baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl)
178	      (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap κ
179	        Γ((baseChangeField C κ).left, baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V))) := by
180	  have hUST : (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)).Opens) ≤ baseChangeFieldMap k κ ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ := le_top
181	  have hUSX : V ≤ C.hom ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ := le_top
182	  have hUY : (baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V) =
183	      baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V ⊓ pullback.snd C.hom (baseChangeFieldMap k κ) ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ := by
184	    simp
185	  have hiso := isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right
186	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback C.hom (baseChangeFieldMap k κ))
187	    hUST hUSX hUY (isAffineOpen_top _) (isAffineOpen_top _) hV hV'
188	  have hpo := (isIso_pushoutSection_iff
189	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback C.hom (baseChangeFieldMap k κ)) hUST hUSX hUY).mp hiso
190	  refine hpo.of_iso (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)) (Iso.refl _)
191	    (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of κ)) (Iso.refl _) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
192	  · simp only [Iso.refl_hom, Category.comp_id]
193	    change _ = _ ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv ≫ _
194	    rw [Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc, Scheme.Hom.appLE]
195	    rfl
196	  · simp only [Scheme.Hom.appLE, Scheme.Hom.preimage_top, homOfLE_refl, op_id,
197	      CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id, Category.comp_id]
198	    exact Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ))
199	  · simp only [Iso.refl_hom, Category.id_comp]
200	    rfl
201	  · simp only [Iso.refl_hom]
202	    change _ = _ ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of κ)).inv ≫ _
203	    rw [Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc, Scheme.Hom.appLE]
204	    rfl
205	
206	/-- **Base change of chart sections along a field extension, as a ring equivalence**:
207	`Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] κ ≃+* Γ(C_κ, fst ⁻¹ᵁ V)`. -/
208	noncomputable def sectionsBaseChangeField {V : C.left.Opens}
209	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set C.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set C.left)) :
210	    Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] κ ≃+* Γ((baseChangeField C κ).left, baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
211	  ((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct k Γ(C.left, V) κ).isoIsPushout _ _
212	    (isPushout_algebraMap_sections_baseChangeField κ hV hV')).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
213	
214	/-- The base-change equivalence on `s ⊗ 1`: it is the pullback of `s` along the first
215	projection `C_κ ⟶ C`.  The computation rule that makes §3 possible. -/
216	theorem sectionsBaseChangeField_tmul_one {V : C.left.Opens}
217	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set C.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set C.left))
218	    (s : Γ(C.left, V)) :
219	    sectionsBaseChangeField κ hV hV' (s ⊗ₜ 1) =
220	      (baseChangeFieldFst C κ).appLE V (baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl s :=
221	  congr($((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct k Γ(C.left, V) κ).inl_isoIsPushout_hom _ _
222	    (isPushout_algebraMap_sections_baseChangeField κ hV hV')).hom s)
223	
224	/-- The base-change equivalence on `1 ⊗ a`: it is the constant `a` of the base-changed curve,
225	i.e. the `κ`-algebra structure map of its sections. -/
226	theorem sectionsBaseChangeField_one_tmul {V : C.left.Opens}
227	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set C.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set C.left)) (a : κ) :
228	    sectionsBaseChangeField κ hV hV' (1 ⊗ₜ a) =
229	      algebraMap κ Γ((baseChangeField C κ).left, baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V) a :=
230	  congr($((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct k Γ(C.left, V) κ).inr_isoIsPushout_hom _ _
231	    (isPushout_algebraMap_sections_baseChangeField κ hV hV')).hom a)
232	
233	/-- The base-change equivalence on a pure tensor `s ⊗ a`: the constant `a` times the pullback
234	of `s`. -/
235	theorem sectionsBaseChangeField_tmul {V : C.left.Opens}
236	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set C.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set C.left))
237	    (s : Γ(C.left, V)) (a : κ) :
238	    sectionsBaseChangeField κ hV hV' (s ⊗ₜ a) =
239	      (baseChangeFieldFst C κ).appLE V (baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl s *
240	        algebraMap κ Γ((baseChangeField C κ).left, baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V) a := by
241	  have h : (s ⊗ₜ[k] a : Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] κ) = (s ⊗ₜ 1) * (1 ⊗ₜ a) := by
242	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one, one_mul]
243	  rw [h, map_mul, sectionsBaseChangeField_tmul_one, sectionsBaseChangeField_one_tmul]
244	
245	/-! ### The `κ`-linear form
246	
247	`BaseSections C 𝒪 V` is *definitionally* `Γ(C.left, V)` (`BaseSections` is a type synonym) and
248	its `k`-module structure is restriction of scalars along `kToSection`, which is the same as the
249	`algebraMap` of `toModuleKSheaf.algebraSection` — so the ring equivalence above already carries
250	the `κ`-linear structure the Čech kit consumes.  `sectionsBaseChangeFieldₗ` records that as a
251	`≃ₗ[κ]` so consumers do not have to re-derive the scalar compatibility. -/
252	
253	/-- **Base change of chart sections along a field extension, `κ`-linearly**:
254	`κ ⊗[k] Γ(C.left, V) ≃ₗ[κ] Γ(C_κ, fst ⁻¹ᵁ V)`.
255	
256	Tensor order note, and it is not cosmetic: `κ` goes on the **left**.  That is the side mathlib's
257	`Module κ (κ ⊗[k] M)` instance and `Module.finrank_baseChange` are keyed on, whereas the pushout
258	of §2 produces the factors the other way round (`Γ ⊗[k] κ`), so the two are bridged by
259	`TensorProduct.comm`.  Writing the equivalence at `Γ ⊗[k] κ ≃ₗ[κ]` does not typecheck at all —
260	there is no `Module κ` on that spelling — which is worth recording because it is the kind of
261	order mismatch that reads like bookkeeping and is actually an instance wall.
262	
263	On the target the `κ`-action is the structure action of `C_κ`'s own structure morphism, i.e.
264	exactly the `Scheme.BaseSections` action of `CohomologyKit` at base field `κ`. -/
265	noncomputable def sectionsBaseChangeFieldₗ {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
266	    {V : C.left.Opens} (hV : IsCompact (V : Set C.left))
267	    (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set C.left)) :
268	    κ ⊗[k] Γ(C.left, V) ≃ₗ[κ]
269	      Γ((baseChangeField C κ).left, baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V) where
270	  toFun x := sectionsBaseChangeField κ hV hV' (TensorProduct.comm k κ Γ(C.left, V) x)
271	  invFun y := (TensorProduct.comm k κ Γ(C.left, V)).symm
272	    ((sectionsBaseChangeField κ hV hV').symm y)
273	  left_inv x := by
274	    simp only [RingEquiv.symm_apply_apply, LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
275	  right_inv y := by
276	    simp only [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
277	  map_add' x y := by rw [map_add, map_add]
278	  map_smul' a x := by
279	    rw [RingHom.id_apply]
280	    induction x with
281	    | zero => simp only [smul_zero, map_zero]
282	    | add u v hu hv => rw [smul_add, map_add, map_add, hu, hv, map_add, map_add, smul_add]
283	    | tmul b s =>
284	      rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, TensorProduct.comm_tmul,
285	        TensorProduct.comm_tmul, sectionsBaseChangeField_tmul,
286	        sectionsBaseChangeField_tmul, map_mul, Algebra.smul_def]
287	      ring
288	
289	/-- Computation rule for the `κ`-linear form on `1 ⊗ s`: the pullback of `s` along the first
290	projection. -/
291	@[simp] lemma sectionsBaseChangeFieldₗ_one_tmul {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
292	    {V : C.left.Opens} (hV : IsCompact (V : Set C.left))
293	    (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set C.left)) (s : Γ(C.left, V)) :
294	    sectionsBaseChangeFieldₗ κ hV hV' (1 ⊗ₜ s) =
295	      (baseChangeFieldFst C κ).appLE V (baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl s := by
296	  change sectionsBaseChangeField κ hV hV' (TensorProduct.comm k κ Γ(C.left, V) (1 ⊗ₜ s)) = _
297	  rw [TensorProduct.comm_tmul, sectionsBaseChangeField_tmul_one]
298	
299	end Pushout
300	
301	/-! ## §3. Compatibility with restriction
302	
303	The one identity that makes the equivalence a *comparison of complexes* rather than a
304	coincidence of dimensions: base-changing then restricting is restricting then base-changing.
305	Both sides are ring maps out of a tensor product, so it suffices to check on pure tensors, and
306	on those it is the naturality of `appLE` in both projections.
307	
308	This is what `Ledger/GenusFieldInvariance.lean` needs in order to identify the base-changed
309	two-term Čech complex of `S.baseChangeField κ` with the base change of the complex of `S`. -/
310	
311	section Restriction
312	
313	variable {C}
314	
315	/-- **Restriction-naturality of the field base change of sections.**  For qcqs opens `W ≤ V` of
316	`C.left`, restricting a base-changed section from `fst ⁻¹ᵁ V` to `fst ⁻¹ᵁ W` is the base change
317	of the restricted section.
318	
319	Stated on the tensor side as a composite with `Algebra.TensorProduct.map (res) (id κ)`, so it
320	can be used to rewrite either way. -/
321	theorem sectionsBaseChangeField_res {V W : C.left.Opens}
322	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set C.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set C.left))
323	    (hW : IsCompact (W : Set C.left)) (hW' : IsQuasiSeparated (W : Set C.left))
324	    (hWV : W ≤ V) (s : Γ(C.left, V)) (a : κ) :
325	    ((baseChangeField C κ).left.presheaf.map
326	        (homOfLE (show baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ W ≤ baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V by
327	          gcongr)).op).hom
328	      (sectionsBaseChangeField κ hV hV' (s ⊗ₜ a)) =
329	      sectionsBaseChangeField κ hW hW'
330	        ((C.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE hWV).op).hom s ⊗ₜ a) := by
331	  rw [sectionsBaseChangeField_tmul, sectionsBaseChangeField_tmul, map_mul]
332	  congr 1
333	  · -- the first-projection pullback is natural in the open: postcomposing the pullback with the
334	    -- downstairs restriction (`appLE_map`) is precomposing with the upstairs one (`map_appLE`)
335	    have h₁ := Scheme.Hom.appLE_map (baseChangeFieldFst C κ)
336	      (le_rfl : baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V ≤ baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V)
337	      (homOfLE (show baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ W ≤ baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V by gcongr)).op
338	    have h₂ := Scheme.Hom.map_appLE (baseChangeFieldFst C κ)
339	      (show baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ W ≤ baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ W from le_rfl)
340	      (homOfLE hWV).op
341	    exact congr($(h₁.trans h₂.symm).hom s)
342	  · -- the constant `a` is unchanged by restriction (`algebraMap` naturality)
343	    exact toModuleKSheaf.algebraMap_naturality (C := baseChangeField C κ) _ a
344	
345	end Restriction
346	
347	/-! ## §4. The dimension consequence, and precisely what it is not
348	
349	`finrank_sections_baseChangeField` is the numerical payoff available *from §2 alone*: the
350	`κ`-dimension of the base-changed chart sections equals the `k`-dimension of the original's,
351	whenever the latter is free (automatic over a field).  This is `Module.finrank_baseChange`
352	composed with the equivalence — no geometry beyond §2.
353	
354	**Read the scope note.**  This is a statement about **chart sections**, i.e. about the terms of
355	the Čech complex.  It is *not* `h¹` invariance and it is *not* the genus identity: those need
356	§3 to identify the *maps*, and then right-exactness of `⊗` to pass to the cokernel.  Publishing
357	the termwise identity as if it were the cohomological one is exactly the conflation this
358	cluster's task exists to prevent, so it is named termwise and its limits are stated here. -/
359	
360	section Dimension
361	
362	variable {C}
363	
364	/-- **The `κ`-dimension of base-changed chart sections is the `k`-dimension of the original's.**
365	
366	Termwise only: `V` is one open, and this says nothing about `H¹`, whose comparison additionally
367	needs §3 and right-exactness.  Free-ness of `Γ(C.left, V)` over `k` is automatic (`k` is a
368	field), which is why there is no hypothesis for it. -/
369	theorem finrank_sections_baseChangeField {V : C.left.Opens}
370	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set C.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set C.left)) :
371	    Module.finrank κ Γ((baseChangeField C κ).left, baseChangeFieldFst C κ ⁻¹ᵁ V) =
372	      Module.finrank k Γ(C.left, V) := by
373	  rw [← (sectionsBaseChangeFieldₗ κ hV hV').finrank_eq, Module.finrank_baseChange]
374	
375	/-- Non-vacuity of §4 in the shape a consumer meets it: on a chart of a 2-affine cover the qcqs
376	hypotheses are discharged by affineness, so the dimension identity fires with no side condition.
377	
378	Stated at `U₁`; `U₂` and `U₁ ⊓ U₂` are identical, and the overlap is the case the Čech `H¹`
379	carrier is built from — `(S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ ⊓ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂` is `rfl`-equal to
380	`fst ⁻¹ᵁ (S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂)`, so this covers every term of the base-changed complex. -/
381	theorem finrank_sections_baseChangeField_chart (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
382	    Module.finrank κ Γ((baseChangeField C κ).left, (S.baseChangeField κ).U₁) =
383	      Module.finrank k Γ(C.left, S.U₁) :=
384	  finrank_sections_baseChangeField κ S.isAffineOpen_U₁.isCompact
385	    S.isAffineOpen_U₁.isQuasiSeparated
386	
387	/-- The same at the overlap `U₁ ⊓ U₂` — the term whose quotient *is* the Čech `Ȟ¹` carrier.
388	Recorded separately because it is the one §5 of a genus-invariance file would consume, and
389	because it makes explicit that the overlap chart of the base-changed cover is the preimage of
390	the overlap (`rfl`, by `AffineCoverMVSquare.preimage`). -/
391	theorem finrank_sections_baseChangeField_overlap (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
392	    Module.finrank κ
393	        Γ((baseChangeField C κ).left,
394	          (S.baseChangeField κ).U₁ ⊓ (S.baseChangeField κ).U₂) =
395	      Module.finrank k Γ(C.left, S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂) :=
396	  finrank_sections_baseChangeField κ S.isAffineOpen_inf.isCompact
397	    S.isAffineOpen_inf.isQuasiSeparated
398	
399	end Dimension
400	
401	end Scheme
402
